title: St. Louis sidemen, Sleepy's trumpet surprise, illness and Springfield
summary: Handy recalls New Orleans men in St. Louis, the second trumpeter who outplayed Guy Kelly, his illness in hospital around 1938-39, and a small band in Springfield.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Did they have many New Orleans grounds up there with those phones?

No. Uh, Gishard, he's from here, but he was playing with another band on the name of Eddie. Eddie something they was playing. He's a saxophone player too, a how-to player. And he had a brother, a dead shawty, played bass, but I think the young ones did the bass play. I think he died. I had a fellow out at, uh, Shreveport with, uh, Goldstone's band. I played a lot of, a lot of, a lot of Tramon too. A little skinny fella. I forget his name too. Fine Tramon player. I only had a guy playing trumpet there, second trumpet. Called him Sleepy. He'd come down here with fate too. That guy wouldn't play nothing but second trumpet. He wouldn't play nothing. And Guy Kelly coming in that night, and Guy and I played a number two with us. And this fella had been sitting up there playing like that for seven to eight months. And Guy came in there and played so much trumpet, man. He'd come in there and played so much trumpet, man. This guy got up and washed Guy out, man. He washed him out. Broke up the house, man. We all had to stop and look at him. Didn't know he was sitting back there for eight or nine months. He didn't play nothing but second. Strictly music. Didn't try to get off at all, you know. Man, all of a sudden he came out that blowing. Well, I stayed at that place until I got sick. Got sick around. 38, 39. I stayed in Homer Phillip Hospital there in St. Louis for three years. And I was sitting back in the back. And I was sitting back in the back. And I was sitting back in the back. And I was sitting back in the back. And I was sitting back in the back. I was sitting back in the back. I was sitting back in the back. I went back down to my job. I had a fellow from here. I died from here. I had a place in Springfield, Illinois. I came up and asked me to come up there and wait for him. I taken six pieces and went up there. Was it six? Five or six. I was a drummer, piano, saxophone. I didn't have no trumpet. That's about all I had. Three pieces. I had two girls singing. Me to five. Two girls were singing.
